title: Finding record, version 2
description: One file per finding: community/findings/<number // 1000>/F<number>.json. A record holds what was observed and the dated evidence of what happened to it. It holds no status: the status is computed from the evidence (the first that applies of closed, fixed_in, answer, sent, repeated with result reproduced; otherwise the finding is filed). `python3 scripts/community.py check` validates every record against this schema and adds the rules a schema cannot express: the file path, the identity rule (above F47 the id is F<issue>), real calendar dates in order, known release ids, a second measurement by someone other than the reporter, Markdown without images, headings or relative links, and references between records.

id.description: Never changes. From F48 on it is F followed by the issue number; F1 to F32 follow an older numbering.

issue.description: The issue in this repository where the finding is discussed, or null.

title.description: What was observed, in one line. No status, no remedy.

kind.description: defect: something in the data looks wrong. question: a question to the provider about what the data means. difference: a difference in method, scope or convention.

datasets.description: Every dataset the finding is about, by code. Empty when the finding is not about listed datasets; then `scope` says what it is about.

scope.description: Free text for what the finding concerns beyond the listed datasets: a group of datasets, a flow, a workbook, a file of a release.

releases.description: Provider releases in which it was observed, as ids from the list in site/config.json.

observation.description: What the data says, what it was compared with, and the question to the provider if there is one. Markdown. Names and single values only, never text from a report.

exposure.description: What it affects, if known: scores, consumers. Markdown; may be empty.

method.description: How it was measured and on which files, and what was not measured. Markdown.

by.description: Who reported it: a GitHub login or a name.

url.description: The issue or thread in which it was reported.

reported.description: Who reported the finding, when and where. Null values are accepted only on the ids that predate this format.

by.description: The second person: a GitHub login or a name. Never the reporter.

url.description: Where the second person says what they got.

repeated.description: The second measurement, by a named second person.

batch.description: Findings reported together share a batch id and its date.

sent.description: When the finding was reported to the provider.

summary.description: The provider's answer in our own words, attributed to the provider. No person's name, no quotation from correspondence.

url.description: A public place where the answer is summarised.

answer.description: The provider's answer. An answer does not correct anything; only `fixed_in` does.

detail.description: The file of that release that carries the correction, when a release has more than one.

date.description: When the correction was checked in that release.

url.description: The public evidence of that check.

fixed_in.description: The provider release that contains the correction, once it has been checked there.

closed.description: Leaves the path: withdrawn (it did not hold when measured again) or not-a-defect (kept for information).

related.description: Other findings this one refers to. One direction is enough; the site shows both.

threads.description: Discussion elsewhere: a thread in another project, or a second issue here.

next.description: The next step and who takes it, for maintainers.

retained.description: Requests to other projects, objections and earlier readings that stay on record.

notes.description: Longer detail. Markdown; may be empty.

raw_html.description: What no text of a record may hold: the site renders records into pages.

release_id.description: The id of a provider release, as site/config.json lists it: the check of the records refuses an id the list does not have.

line.description: One line without a table bar: it is shown in tables.

code.description: The dataset number in the provider's release.

role.description: subject (the default): the observation is in this dataset. affected: a result of this dataset changes because it uses a subject dataset. named: named in the finding as a supplier or for comparison.
